51604271.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant human TLR7 assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis
51604271.references_previous: J. Ou, L. Zheng, Y. Chen, Q. Fu, L. Tan, E. Liang, L. Huang, Y. Pan, J. Ke, Z. Chen, K. Cheng, Heterocyclic-modified imidazoquinoline derivatives: selective TLR7 agonist regulates tumor microenvironment against melanoma, J. Med. Chem. 67 (2024) 3321–3338.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - SPR assay [30]: SPR assay was performed on a Biacore™ 1K SPR system (Cytiva) using the sensor chip CM5 (Cytiva). Briefly, recombinant human TLR7 protein (Catalog number: YA7803H, AtaGenix) solution was coated on the surface of the sensor chip at a dose of 50 μg/mL. Loading and recycling buffer were prepared in advance. The test compound 11a was fresh prepared by dissolving in the loading buffer with the final dose of 3.90, 7.81, 15.62, 31.25, 62.50 or 125.00 μM. SPR data was analyzed using the Biacore insight evaluation Software.
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Fig. 5. SPR analysis of 11a binding to recombinant human TLR7 protein. The indicated doses of 11a (3.90, 7.81, 15.62, 31.25, 62.50 or 125.00 μM) were injected over the sensor chip pre-immobilized with TLR7 protein, and then SPR analysis was conducted on the Biacore™ 1K system. Data was analyzed using the Biacore insight evaluation Software.
original_paragraph.Results - Binding analysis of 11a and TL: To investigate whether 11a could bind with TLR7 directly, we then analyzed the interaction between 11a and TLR7 by using surface plasmon resonance (SPR) spectroscopy as previously described [30]. SPR result indicated that 11a can bind well to the recombinant human TLR7 protein with a calculated K_D value of 7.06 μM (Fig. 5).
